Catalan

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from French brigade.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): (Central, Balearic) [bɾiˈɣa.ðə]
  • IPA(key): (Valencia) [bɾiˈɣa.ða]

Noun

[edit]

brigada f (plural brigades)

  1. brigade

Derived terms

[edit]
  • brigadista

Related terms

[edit]
  • brigadier

Further reading

[edit]
  • “brigada”, in Diccionari de la llengua catalana [Dictionary of the Catalan Language] (in Catalan), second edition, Institute of Catalan Studies [Catalan: Institut d'Estudis Catalans], April 2007

brigada

Galician

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Ultimately from French brigade.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [bɾiˈɣaðɐ]

Noun

[edit]

brigada f (plural brigadas)

  1. (military) brigade (military unit composed of several regiments)
  2. team, squad

References

[edit]
  • Antón Luís Santamarina Fernández, editor (2006–2013), “brigada”, in Dicionario de Dicionarios da lingua galega [Dictionary of Dictionaries of the Galician language] (in Galician), Santiago de Compostela: Instituto da Lingua Galega
  • Antón Luís Santamarina Fernández, Ernesto Xosé González Seoane, María Álvarez de la Granja, editors (2003–2018), “brigada”, in Tesouro informatizado da lingua galega (in Galician), Santiago de Compostela: Instituto da Lingua Galega
  • Rosario Álvarez Blanco, editor (2014–2024), “brigada”, in Tesouro do léxico patrimonial galego e portugués (in Galician), Santiago de Compostela: Instituto da Lingua Galega, →ISSN

Ingrian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Russian бригада (brigada).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Ala-Laukaa) IPA(key): /ˈbriɡɑdɑ/, [ˈbriɡɑˑd]
  • (Soikkola) IPA(key): /ˈbriɡɑːdɑ/, [ˈprikˑɑːd̥ɑ]
  • Rhymes: -iɡɑd, -iɡɑːdɑ
  • Hyphenation: bri‧ga‧da

Noun

[edit]

brigada

  1. brigade

Declension

[edit]
Declension of brigada (type 3/kana, no gradation)
singular plural
nominative brigada brigadat
genitive brigadan brigadoin
partitive brigadaa brigadoja
illative brigadaa brigadoihe
inessive brigadaas brigadois
elative brigadast brigadoist
allative brigadalle brigadoille
adessive brigadaal brigadoil
ablative brigadalt brigadoilt
translative brigadaks brigadoiks
essive brigadanna, brigadaan brigadoinna, brigadoin
exessive1) brigadant brigadoint
1) obsolete
*) the accusative corresponds with either the genitive (sg) or nominative (pl)
**) the comitative is formed by adding the suffix -ka? or -kä? to the genitive.

References

[edit]
  • Arvo Laanest (1978), Isuri keele ajalooline foneetika ja morfoloogia [The historical phonology and morphology of the Ingrian language]‎[2], Tallinn, page 25

  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /bɾiˈɡa.dɐ/

Portuguese brigada

    Borrowed from French brigade.[1]

    Noun

    [edit]

    brigada f (plural brigadas)

    1. (military) brigade (military unit composed of several regiments)
    2. brigade (group of people)
    Derived terms
    [edit]
    • brigadeiro
    • brigadiano
    • brigadista
    Descendants
    [edit]
    • → Javanese: ꦧꦽꦒꦢ (bregada)
      • → Indonesian: bregada

    Etymology 2

    [edit]

    Clipping of obrigada.

    Interjection

    [edit]

    brigada f

    1. (colloquial, women's speech) thanks

    Etymology 3

    [edit]

    See the etymology of the corresponding lemma form.

    Participle

    [edit]

    brigada f sg

    1. feminine singular of brigado

    Serbo-Croatian

    [edit]

    Noun

    [edit]

    brigada f (Cyrillic spelling бригада)

    1. brigade

    Spanish

    [edit]

    Etymology

    [edit]

    Borrowed from French brigade.

    Pronunciation

    [edit]
    • IPA(key): /bɾiˈɡada/ [bɾiˈɣ̞a.ð̞a]
    • Rhymes: -ada
    • Syllabification: bri‧ga‧da

    Noun

    [edit]

    brigada f (plural brigadas)

    1. team, squad (organized group)
    2. (military) brigade, a large military unit, smaller than a division, consisting of several regiments or battalions

    Derived terms

    [edit]
    • brigada de bomberos

    Further reading

    [edit]
    • “brigada”, in Diccionario de la lengua española [Dictionary of the Spanish Language] (in Spanish), online version 23.8.1, Royal Spanish Academy [Spanish: Real Academia Española], 15 December 2025
